corpus.note_on_top_lists: top lists were built twice during iteration (initial object-dtype bug + fixed version), deduped afterwards
corpus.filters: dropped docs with <2 tokens after cleaning (=112) and exact (source_key, lower(title)) duplicates (=50940)

method.text_recipe: per plan: source-specific field concatenation, lowered, separators/punctuation -> space, feat./ft. removed, pure-number tokens dropped
method.tfidf: TfidfVectorizer(max_features=5000, stop_words='english') on final corpus -> (145435, 5000) sparse, L2-normalized
method.kmeans: KMeans(n_clusters=10, random_state=42, n_init=10) on the TF-IDF matrix; inertia=137541.85
method.lda: LatentDirichletAllocation(n_components=10, random_state=42) fitted on the SAME TF-IDF matrix (non-standard input but required by the single-vectorization spec); perplexity=4261.66
method.dominant_topic: argmax of the cluster-mean LDA doc-topic distribution
method.coherence_score: mean cosine similarity between cluster docs and its KMeans centroid; clusters >500 docs sampled to 500 with np.random.seed(42)
method.representative_items: top 5 by cosine similarity to centroid over the FULL cluster (titles deduped, '|'->'/', truncated to 120 chars), 'source: title' joined with ' | '

interpretation.topic_space: 8 of 10 LDA topics are dominated by Spotify genre/language tokens (pop, cantopop, metal, malay, ao vivo, hop...), because Spotify accounts for ~50% of docs and genre tokens are repeated twice for weighting; topics 8 and 9 capture film/TV vocabulary (drama, comedy, films, documentary, tv).
interpretation.clusters: Clusters 1-4 and 7 are tight music-genre clusters (coherence 0.52-0.66). Cluster 0 is a very large, low-coherence 'generic Spotify pop/rock' bucket (0.089) that received nearly all remaining short music docs. Clusters 5/6/8/9 are the cross-source buckets (Netflix drama/comedy, movies overviews+production companies, books, video games by platform/publisher) and land on the film/TV or pop/eng topics with low-to-mid coherence, i.e. the topic space is music-skewed while the cluster space separates media types on TF-IDF vocabulary.
caveats: LDA fitted on TF-IDF (not raw counts) is mathematically non-standard; required by spec to use one vectorization.
Dedup by (source, title) collapsed 114k Spotify rows to 72k, since identical track names by different artists were merged.
No 2017-2020 hard filtering: only ~1% of movies/books/games fall in that window and Spotify has no year column (per data_profile/plan).
